function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Java** is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was first released by Sun Microsystems in 1995 (now owned by Oracle). It’s designed to be:

| Feature | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Write once, run anywhere (WORA)** | Java programs compile to bytecode that runs on any device with a Java Virtual Machine (JVM). |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives), encouraging modular, reusable code. |
| **Strongly typed** | Types are checked at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Garbage collector frees developers from manual memory deallocation. |
| **Platform‑independent** | Same source code works on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, embedded devices, etc. |
| **Rich standard library** | Collections, I/O, networking, concurrency, GUI (Swing/JavaFX), database access (JDBC), etc. |
| **Secure** | JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and a robust security manager. |

---

### Quick History

| Year | Milestone |
|------|-----------|
| 1991 | James Gosling and team start “Green Project” at Sun. |
| 1995 | Java 1.0 released – “Java is fun, fast, and portable.” |
| 1998 | Java 2 (J2SE 1.2) introduces Swing, JDBC, and the Java Development Kit (JDK). |
| 2004 | Java 5 (J2SE 5.0) adds generics, annotations, enhanced for‑loop, etc. |
| 2010 | Oracle acquires Sun Microsystems. |
| 2017 | Java 9 introduces modules (Project Jigsaw). |
| 2023 | Java 21 (LTS) – latest long‑term support release. |

---

### Typical Use Cases

| Domain | Why Java? |
|--------|-----------|
| **Enterprise applications** | Robust, scalable, mature ecosystem (Spring, Hibernate). |
| **Android apps** | Android SDK uses Java (or Kotlin, which interoperates). |
| **Web servers & microservices** | Tomcat, Jetty, Spring Boot, Quarkus. |
| **Big data** | Hadoop, Spark (Java APIs). |
| **Desktop GUIs** | Swing, JavaFX. |
| **Embedded systems** | Java ME, Android Things. |
| **Financial services** | Low‑latency trading, risk engines. |

---

### A Tiny “Hello, World!” Example

```java
// File: HelloWorld.java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, World!");
    }
}
```

Compile & run:

```bash
javac HelloWorld.java   # compiles to HelloWorld.class (bytecode)
java HelloWorld         # JVM executes the bytecode
```

---

### Common Misconceptions

| Myth | Reality |
|------|---------|
| **Java = JavaScript** | Completely different languages; JavaScript is a scripting language for browsers. |
| **Java is slow** | Modern JVMs use Just‑In‑Time (JIT) compilation and optimizations; performance rivals native code for many workloads. |
| **Java is only for desktop** | It powers servers, mobile (Android), embedded, cloud, and even IoT devices. |

---

### Getting Started

1. **Install JDK** (Java Development Kit) – e.g., AdoptOpenJDK, Oracle JDK, or OpenJDK.
2. **Choose an IDE** – IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code (with Java extensions).
3. **Learn the basics** – classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces, collections, exception handling.
4. **Explore frameworks** – Spring Boot for web services, Hibernate for ORM, JavaFX for UI.

---

### Resources

| Type | Link |
|------|------|
| Official docs | https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/ |
| Tutorials | https://www.tutorialspoint.com/java/ |
| Community | https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/java |
| Courses | Coursera, Udemy, edX (Java Programming & Software Engineering Fundamentals) |

---

**Bottom line:** Java is a versatile, mature language that lets you write code once and run it anywhere—from enterprise servers to Android phones—thanks to its virtual machine, rich libraries, and strong community support.
